title: Keema Naan Flatbreads
subtitle: Stuffed lamb mince flatbreads cooked in a frying pan
excerpt: Keema naan is a spiced minced lamb filling cooked and pressed inside a yoghurt flatbread dough, then fried in a dry pan until blistered and golden. No tandoor oven needed. The dough uses self-raising flour and Greek yoghurt for a quick no-yeast result.
sourceNotes: Keema naan is a popular Indian restaurant bread stuffed with spiced mince. In restaurants it is baked on the wall of a tandoor. This pan-cooked version uses a yoghurt dough that puffs and blisters in a hot dry pan, mimicking the effect.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the keema filling up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Make the dough fresh.

content.text: Press the naan down hard with a spatula as it cooks to ensure good contact with the pan. The blisters form where the dough touches the hot surface directly.
Make the dough: mix flour and yoghurt together with a pinch of salt until a soft dough forms. Knead for 2 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes under a damp cloth.
Cook the keema: fry the onion in a little oil for 5 minutes. Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute. Add the lamb mince and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until browned and dry.
Add the cumin, coriander, garam masala, and chilli flakes. Stir and cook for 1 minute. Season well. Stir in the fresh coriander. Cool slightly.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces. Roll one piece into a thin round, about 20cm.
Place a quarter of the keema filling on one half of the round. Fold the other half over and press the edges to seal. Roll gently again to flatten into an oval.
Cook in a hot dry frying pan for 3 to 4 minutes each side, pressing down with a spatula, until golden and blistered.
Brush with ghee immediately. Repeat with the remaining dough and filling. Serve hot.

items.fix: Press dough edges together firmly; roll gently after folding.

items.symptom: Dough is sticky and hard to roll.
items.fix: Dust generously with flour when rolling.
